sections.heading: 1. Easier on the back
lines: ① Short strokes close to you, feet following.
② One foot forward, lunge stance, shift weight.
③ Handle height with elbows slightly bent.
④ Break every 1–2 rooms; swap front foot.

get checked. Bladder or bowel changes: doctor now.

caption:
Koko's back grumbles after every big clean. Usually it's not the bending itself. It's the long, reaching strokes and the unbroken stints.

A few tweaks help. Take short strokes close to your body and walk with the vacuum. Use a lunge stance and shift your weight forward and back. Adjust the handle so you can stand taller with elbows slightly bent. Then break it up: one or two rooms, a quick walk or a cuppa, and swap your front foot.

Leg pain, numbness, weakness or pain building over a week or two is worth an assessment, and any bladder or bowel change needs a doctor straight away. Our chiropractors can help. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
